```{r}
library(fpp3)
library(USgas)

#3. US natural gas data:

# ?us_total #US Annual Total Natural Gas Consumption per state

us_total_tsibble <- us_total %>%
  as_tsibble(index = year, key = state)


#Filtering the data to get New England states:

new_england <- us_total_tsibble %>%
  filter(state %in% c(        # %in% says check if 'state' is in c(......)
    "Maine",
    "Vermont",
    "New Hampshire",
    "Massachusetts",
    "Connecticut",
    "Rhode Island"
  ))

new_england %>%
  autoplot(y) +
  labs(                                           
    title = "Annual Natural Gas Consumption in New England",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Natural Gas Consumption"
  )

# Comments on your finding:

# scale difference is so big for example Vermont is too small comparing to other to see anything
# it will be better to have separate graphs, one for each state


```

labs() : labs() is used to modify the labels and title of your plot

In labs() you can modify:

title → graph title
x → x-axis label
y → y-axis label
subtitle → subtitle
caption → caption at the bottom

example -->

labs(
  title = "Pharmaceutical Costs",
  subtitle = "Concessional co-payments, ATC1 A, ATC2 A01",
  x = "Month",
  y = "Cost ($)"
)
